cues.say: Component 12: Rate limits. A cap on how often one person or machine can call you. Extra requests get an instant slow down error. You'll bring this up during the spike defenses.
Think of it as: A bouncer letting each person through once a minute. Use it for bots, retry storms, and provider limits.
Here's a real scenario. A reseller's script hits checkout 300 times a second from one IP. A buggy app retries in a tight loop.
Without it: The script floods servers and buys the stock.
The retry loop turns a hiccup into an outage.
With it: Edge cap of 10 a second per IP: 290 rejected before the servers.
Business cap: 1 per customer per item, across IPs.
The retry loop gets slow down errors, not the database.
Why it works: It protects real customers fair share, and the servers.
In the interview, say: Per IP at the edge, and 2 orders per phone in the API.
A few related terms you may hear.
429: The too many requests error code.
WAF: Web application firewall: blocks known attacks and bots.
DDoS protection: Absorbs floods of junk traffic. WAF and DDoS come with the CDN: mention them, don't design them.
